audit_findings.title: Consolidated cash-flow add-backs may belong partly to noncontrolling owners
audit_findings.magnitude: unquantified (filed 2025 noncontrolling-interest income was $24.2 million, 39.5% of the $61.3 million anchor; distributions to noncontrolling interests were $18.2 million)
audit_findings.mechanism: Parent-attributable earnings are combined with consolidated D&A, working-capital changes, capital expenditure, disposal proceeds, and other cash-flow adjustments, potentially changing anchor OE and every projected year.
audit_findings.evidence: The noncontrolling interest included in the accompanying Consolidated Balance Sheets represents the non-Trinity equity interest in these partially-owned subsidiaries.
audit_findings.explanation: The filing demonstrates that material noncontrolling ownership existed, but the supplied record does not demonstrate that the OE bridge used inconsistent ownership bases. If parent earnings were adjusted with wholly consolidated cash flows, excess add-backs would overstate value while excess capital deductions could understate it. The filed NCI amounts are large relative to the anchor, so the possible mismatch is reasonably capable of materially changing the valuation.
audit_findings.action: Rebuild the 2025 OE bridge by legal entity and ownership percentage, allocating D&A, working capital, fleet investment, sale proceeds, interest, taxes, and NCI distributions consistently to Trinity common shareholders, then rerun all scenarios without changing other assumptions.

audit_findings.title: The December 2025 restructuring makes reported 2025 earnings an invalid steady-state perimeter
audit_findings.magnitude: unquantified (6,235 railcars became wholly owned and 10,850 became investor owned in December 2025; 17,025 railcars had moved from partially owned to investor owned across the partnership transactions by June 2026)
audit_findings.mechanism: The restructuring changes the parent share of leasing revenue, operating costs, interest, capital spending, disposal economics, and NCI allocations used to establish sustainable OE.
audit_findings.evidence: The financial results of RIV 2013 will continue to be consolidated in our Consolidated Financial Statements but will no longer be subject to a noncontrolling interest adjustment as a result of the Exchange Transaction.
audit_findings.explanation: This is a demonstrated perimeter mismatch: the $61.3 million anchor represents predominantly pre-transaction 2025 ownership, while the valuation has a null perimeter adjustment and is dated after both the December 2025 and April 2026 partnership transactions. The direction cannot be established because Trinity gained the remaining RIV interest while divesting Triumph and later TRIP interests. The affected fleet is sufficiently large that a post-transaction anchor could materially differ from reported 2025 OE.
audit_findings.action: Prepare a pro forma parent-attributable OE statement using the June 30, 2026 perimeter: fully include RIV 2013, exclude the divested Triumph and TRIP operations and debt service, include only Trinity's equity-method interests and servicing income, and rerun the valuation.

audit_findings.title: The anchor may retain a material noncash divestiture gain
audit_findings.magnitude: $194.2 million pre-tax, equal to 3.17 times the $61.3 million OE anchor
audit_findings.mechanism: Any surviving divestiture gain inflates anchor OE and is then capitalized through the explicit forecast and terminal value.
audit_findings.evidence: As a result of the divestiture of Triumph, the Company recognized a non-cash pre-tax gain of $194.2 million during the year ended December 31, 2025, and Triumph and its related debt are no longer included in our Consolidated Financial Statements.
audit_findings.explanation: The filing's GAAP cash-flow reconciliation explicitly subtracts the full $194.2 million gain, so retention in OE is not a demonstrated error. The exact OE bridge is not supplied, however, leaving unresolved whether the gain, its tax effects, disposal proceeds, or related working-capital entries re-entered elsewhere. Because the filed gain exceeds three times the anchor, even partial survival could materially alter the valuation.
audit_findings.action: Trace the $194.2 million gain from net income through every OE adjustment, separately reconcile taxes, the $69.2 million of divested noncash net assets, consideration received, restricted cash, and disposal proceeds, and rerun if any portion affected recurring OE.

audit_findings.title: Railcar purchases, sales, and gains can be double-counted or misclassified as maintenance economics
audit_findings.magnitude: unquantified (filed 2025 amounts: $749.3 million fleet capital expenditure, $399.3 million portfolio-sale proceeds, $91.4 million sale gains, and $350.0 million net fleet investment)
audit_findings.mechanism: Classification and duplication of fleet purchases, sale proceeds, disposal gains, and maintenance versus growth capital directly change OE and the reinvestment required to support forecast growth.
audit_findings.evidence: For the year ended December 31, 2025, we made a net fleet investment of approximately $350.0 million, which primarily includes new railcar additions, railcar modifications, and other betterments, net of deferred profit, as well as secondary market purchases; and is net of proceeds from lease portfolio sales.
audit_findings.explanation: No specific double count is demonstrated because the exact OE bridge and maintenance-capital calculation are absent. The exposure is nevertheless material: each filed fleet-flow measure is multiple times the $61.3 million anchor. Crediting both proceeds and gains would overstate value, while deducting gross fleet investment without consistent proceeds or treating growth investment as maintenance could substantially understate it.
audit_findings.action: Produce a transaction-level reconciliation from gross fleet additions to $350.0 million net fleet investment, identifying portfolio-sale proceeds, book values, gains, deferred intercompany profit, maintenance and compliance expense, and maintenance versus growth capital; then rerun OE using each cash flow exactly once.

audit_findings.title: The $165.6 million stakes addition is not reconciled to the filing's disclosed unconsolidated investments
audit_findings.magnitude: $165.6 million added to the bridge; $161.9 million of June 30, 2026 equity-method investments is computed from filed amounts of $124.3 million and $37.6 million, leaving $3.7 million unreconciled; the full addition equals $1.98 per share and 14.0% of base equity value
audit_findings.mechanism: Unconsolidated stakes enter the equity bridge, but their earnings may also enter OE; wrong ownership, obligations, or inclusion of consolidated assets can create a direct bridge overstatement or double count.
audit_findings.evidence: At December 31, 2025, the carrying value of these investments totaled $15.1 million.
audit_findings.explanation: The latest filing substantially resolves the original comparison with the older $15.1 million balance because it reports $124.3 million in railcar-partnership investments and $37.6 million in the India joint venture. It does not reconcile the exact $165.6 million addition or show that equity-method earnings were purged from OE. The possible exposure extends beyond the $3.7 million numerical difference if the underlying affiliate earnings and carrying values are both capitalized, so the bridge remains materially unresolved.
audit_findings.action: Map the $165.6 million to each June 30, 2026 investment, ownership percentage, carrying value, associated obligations, and any valuation adjustment; trace equity-method income and servicing income through OE, remove any duplicate earnings or consolidated assets, and rerun the bridge.

audit_findings.title: Recurring retained highway-product costs may have been stripped as discontinued operations
audit_findings.magnitude: $7.2 million after tax in 2025, 11.7% of the $61.3 million anchor; $5.7 million after tax was incurred in the first half of 2026; if omitted and capitalized at the 2025 level, the computed base-value effect is approximately $101.1 million or $1.21 per share
audit_findings.mechanism: Excluding continuing cash costs associated with retained indemnity and litigation obligations raises anchor OE and every forecast and terminal cash flow.
audit_findings.evidence: For the years ended December 31, 2025, 2024, and 2023, we recorded expenses related to these obligations of $9.9 million ($7.2 million, net of income taxes), $18.4 million ($14.3 million, net of income taxes), and $17.0 million ($13.4 million, net of income taxes), respectively.
audit_findings.explanation: The recurring cash burden is demonstrated by filed after-tax costs of $13.4 million in 2023, $14.3 million in 2024, $7.2 million in 2025, and $5.7 million during the first half of 2026. Whether the $61.3 million OE bridge retained those costs is unresolved. Their repeated occurrence and scale relative to the anchor make omission materially capable of overstating value, notwithstanding their discontinued-operations classification.
audit_findings.action: Confirm whether the 2025 $7.2 million after-tax cash outflow is included in anchor OE, develop a continuing allowance using the retained-obligation record and subsequent 2026 spending, and rerun all scenarios with that allowance deducted.
